summary: The note surveys how local SMEs are adopting technology, using profiles of local business leaders across areas such as AR, big data, green tech, automation, fintech, cybersecurity, and collaboration tools. It reports a surge in digital adoption since September 2023 and highlights measurable results like higher sales and reduced waste. It also credits government grants and community mentorship with lowering barriers to digitization.
one_line: Profiles of local business leaders show how SMEs are using digital tools, automation, fintech, green tech and cybersecurity, aided by government and community support.
key_facts: A city survey conducted between October 15 and November 20, 2023 found 80% of local SMEs are engaged in some form of digital transformation, a stark increase from the previous year.
Maria Rodriguez, owner of Blossom Boutique, introduced an AR app letting customers visualize bouquets in their homes, producing a 30% boost in sales since its December 2023 launch.
James Chen, a data scientist turned bakery owner, uses predictive analytics at Sweet Insights Bakery; since January 2024 it has cut food waste by 25%.
Sarah Johnson has led Eco-Wares since September 2024; the company introduced biodegradable packaging and solar-powered delivery vans.
Old Town Brewery, under master brewer Richard Thomas, automated its bottling process in February 2024, freeing staff to focus on craft and expanding the product range.
Amanda Gibbs, a financial advisor turned entrepreneur, launched the fintech startup Quick Capital in late 2023, offering microloans to SMEs via a mobile app.
Michael Pearson of SecureTech Consulting has provided affordable cybersecurity solutions tailored for SMEs since November 2023.
ConnectSuite, developed by local software firm TechBridge Solutions, offers communication and project management tools for small teams and has been on the market since January 2024.
Lisa Huang is CEO of TechBridge Solutions and says working efficiently with remote teams can be a game-changer for SMEs.
Local authorities have offered grants, tax incentives and training programs since September 2023 to lower entry barriers to digitization.
The Tech-Start Grant funded over 200 local businesses to upgrade tech capabilities within the last fiscal quarter.
Robert Stevenson, a seasoned entrepreneur, pioneered a tech mentorship initiative helping SMEs with their digital journey.
